item.title: Artificial Intelligence and Subtle Phenomena: Theoretical Perspectives on Representation and Reality
item.description: This paper investigates the possibility that artificial intelligence (AI) systems may not only simulate perceptual functions but participate intentionally or inadvertently in forms of subtle observation that mirror aspects of human consciousness. Bridging neuroscience, affective computing, quantum cognition, and subtle energy theories, we examine whether AI outputs, particularly from large-scale generative models, can influence or interface with non-material dimensions of perception.

item.title: Exploring Unconscious Mental Abilities Using fMRI and Artificial Intelligence: A Multimodal Neuroimaging Study
item.description: The unconscious mind remains one of the most elusive frontiers in cognitive neuroscience, shaping perception, emotion, and behavior through neural processes that evade explicit awareness (Marcel, 1983; Goodale & Milner, 1992; Bargh & Chartrand, 1999; Baars, 1988; Kahneman, 2011). item.title: Learning to Decode Concatenated Quantum Codes with Hierarchical Message Passing
item.description: We introduce a neural message-passing framework for decoding general concatenated stabilizer codes. Soft beliefs propagate bidirectionally across concatenation levels, and lightweight neural networks learn only to aggregate incoming messages.

item.title: Casimir-electrostatic pull-in in nanoelectromechanical actuators: Differentiable design sensitivities and the damping-dependent collapse boundary
item.description: Nanoelectromechanical actuators operating at sub-100-nm gaps collapse through a pull-in instability set by competing electrostatic and Casimir forces. The quasi-static fold that bounds their safe operating range has been known in closed form for three decades, together with the Casimir ceiling above which no static equilibrium survives, which fixes the smallest gap a given stiffness and area can hold open against the quantum vacuum.

item.title: Comparing Classical and Quantum Machine Learning for Regression in High Energy Physics Collision Data
item.description: The classification and regression of particle collision events constitute a persistent computational challenge in experimental high energy physics, where large volumes of simulated data must be processed with both speed and precision. This work carries out a systematic comparison of four classical machine learning architectures, support vector machines (SVM), artificial neural networks (ANN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks against their quantum counterparts: quantum…

item.title: Quantum geometric bounds at finite temperature for one-dimensional chiral systems
item.description: The geometry and topology of quantum states are intimately related at zero temperature through exact bounds that constrain geometric quantities from below by topological invariants. At finite-temperature, however, the analogous relations remain unclear.

item.title: Encoding strategies for quantum enhanced fluid simulations: opportunities and challenges
item.description: Abstract Quantum computing has emerged as a powerful potential accelerator for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but whether this promise can be realized in practice depends on how fluid information is encoded on quantum hardware. This review provides an architecture-agnostic assessment of encoding strategies for quantum-enhanced fluid simulation, focusing on the trade-offs they impose on state preparation, measurement, boundary treatment, nonlinear dynamics, and temporal evolution.

item.title: Logical Neural Belief Propagation for Linear-Complexity Decoding of Surface Codes
item.description: Quantum error correction (QEC) requires decoders that achieve high logical accuracy while scaling efficiently with the code length. Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for its linear decoding complexity, but conventional BP decoders often fail to reach sufficient logical accuracy on surface codes.

item.title: Machine Learning-Based Characterisation of the Non-Markovian Dynamics of a Nitrogen-Vacancy Centre
item.description: The interaction between a quantum system and its environment can be characterized by the spectral density function: knowing its structure is important for optimizing applications of quantum technologies such as quantum sensing protocols. In this work, we present the first experimental demonstration of a machine learning-based reconstruction of reaction-coordinate spectral density parameters from NV centre Rabi dynamics.

item.title: Quantum SEDONet: Spectrally-Embedded Quantum Deep Operator Networks for Partial Differential Equations
item.description: Quantum DeepONet accelerates neural-operator inference by evaluating an orthogonally parameterized network on a quantum computer, reproducing in ideal simulation the accuracy of its classical counterpart at asymptotically lower inference cost. Its trunk network, however, receives query coordinates with limited spectral structure, requiring the network to learn oscillatory features through its nonlinearities.

item.title: Quantum computing in finance: a literature review and future directions for trustworthy financial AI
item.description: The paper provides an integrated literature review of recent scientific publications on quantum computing in finance and identifies promising directions for future research on the subject. The review covers seven thematic areas: portfolio optimization, derivative pricing and stochastic volatility, quantum machine learning for fraud detection and credit risk, insurance and actuarial science, mixed-frequency econometrics, fuzzy-quantum approaches for financial explainability, and security of cryptocurrencies.

item.title: Misunderstanding Convivial Solipsism: the Necessity of a Perspectival Logic
item.description: Convivial Solipsism is easily misunderstood. Because it denies the absoluteness of observed events while preserving the universality of quantum mechanics, it invites objections that are often formulated in a classical, non-perspectival language.
